summary: Eviatar Shulman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1999–2008), where he later held posts in 2009 and served as department chairman around 2011.

Eyal Aviv specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Utrecht and Leiden under Willem Caland, C. C. Uhlenbeck, and Nicolaas van Wijk, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Leiden (1939–1972).

Fa Qing is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his dissertation at the University of Calgary, studying under Leslie S. Kawamura, Anthony W. Barber, Ronald Neufeldt, Eliezer Segal, Wayne O. McCready, Xiaojie Yang, and K. L. Dhammajoti.

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD under Pierre-Étienne Will at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1993–1999) and became maître de conférences at École Française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

Fabio Rambelli works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Venice, Naples, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and has held posts at Sapporo University (2001–2002) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (around 2009).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the Federigo Enriques Department of Mathematics (1969–2004). She held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1992–2001) and the University of Florence (~2001).
Fafang (1904–1951) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-Kuei Li was a linguist, sinologist, and Tibetologist. He studied at Tsinghua, Michigan, and Chicago, working under Edward Sapir. His career included posts at Academia Sinica, Yale, Harvard, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and the University of Hawaiʻi.
Faren works in Buddhist and religious studies. Faren earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Farzand Ali Durrani was a historian and archaeologist. After studying at the University of Peshawar, University of the Punjab, and University of London, he served as a professor at the University of Peshawar (~1960–1993).
Fausto Gherardo Fumi (1840–1915) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Giuseppe Bardelli at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1858–1862).

Fawad Khan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an archaeology Master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, later serving as Assistant Curator at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Directorate of Archaeology and Museums.

Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery, Wuchang Buddhist Institute, and under Taixu and Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and held leadership roles at the Buddhist Academy of China.

Ferdinand Christian Baur (1792–1860) was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen and the Tübinger Stift (~1809–1814) and later held a post at the University of Tübingen (~1826–1860).

Ferdinand Hitzig (1807–1875) was a religious studies scholar and linguist. He studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829) and later held posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and habilitated at Marburg, where he served as associate professor (1865), full professor (1869), and rector (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing was a scholar of Tibetology, sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Peking University, China Medical University, Humboldt University, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and UC Berkeley (~1935–1952).

Ferdinand Sommer was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate under Rudolf Thurneysen at Freiburg. He held professorships at the universities of Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Geneva, Leipzig (PhD 1880), Berlin, and Paris. He taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1881–1891) and the University of Geneva (1891–1913).
